findings.reason: The authenticated Sales schema makes product_id a primary key, so each product has at most one sales interval. The protected query is correct, but duplicates the overlap predicate and amount calculation in three UNION ALL branches and then groups rows that cannot duplicate under the source key. The candidate represents the three fixed years once, performs one interval-overlap join, and emits each already-unique product-year row directly. This materially improves concision, reviewability, and interview explanation while preserving the required complexity.

The three-row years CTE covers the complete legal date domain. Its closed-interval predicate selects exactly the years touched by each sales interval; taking the later start and earlier end, adding one inclusive day, and multiplying by the daily amount computes exactly that year's contribution. The Sales primary key makes every surviving product-year pair unique, Product supplies the matching name, and the final two-column ordering satisfies the source contract.

The protected SQLite query and immutable MySQL query are correct on every source-valid database tested. The protected query passed all seven ordinary cases, all three benchmark outputs, and repeated scaling verdicts; its branch duplication and unnecessary aggregation are clarity defects rather than semantic failures. Its exact bytes and verified submission evidence remain unchanged, and the improvement exists only as an inert candidate.

An independent Python oracle joined Sales to Product by product_id, intersected each inclusive interval separately with the three calendar years, and sorted the resulting rows by product_id and year. It agreed on all seven visible cases and all three benchmarks with the candidate, protected SQLite source, exact immutable MySQL source executed with its DATEDIFF/LEAST/GREATEST functions supplied, and a separately written de-indexed correlated control.

Seed 1384 generated 5,000 schema-valid databases containing 26,780 Sales rows. Coverage included 332 empty Product tables, 455 empty Sales tables, 3,669 databases with unsold products, 3,909 with duplicate product names, 505 one-day intervals, 3,245 zero-rate intervals, 9,944 leap-day overlaps, 13,366 cross-year intervals, 3,863 intervals spanning all three years, and shuffled storage order. Candidate, protected, exact native, and correlated control matched the oracle throughout.

Across three real-test repetitions, the candidate passed all seven correctness cases, all three benchmark outputs, and scaling with extra growth exponent +0.06 through +0.07 and largest-tier ratio 0.83x through 0.85x. The protected query also passed at -0.00 through +0.01 and 0.99x through 1.00x. The correct de-indexed correlated control passed every output but failed only scaling each time, at +0.68 through +0.70 and 5.71x through 6.13x.

All three benchmark cases remain explicitly hidden and performance-only, use positive unique sizes 32, 128, and 512 for a 16x span, and define size consistently as combined Product and Sales rows. Their 16, 64, and 256 primary-key-matched sales intervals exercise join scaling while completing normally for the slower control. Repeated optimal-class passes and correlated-class scaling-only failures prove the calibration is sound, so benchmark.json was not edited.

The complete Approach now targets the candidate and derives the fixed years relation, closed-interval overlap test, inclusive intersection arithmetic, and elimination of aggregation from the Sales primary key. It proves exact day coverage, states O(P + S + R) time and O(P + S) space, and covers per-year UNION branches, day expansion, correlated scans, unnecessary grouping, inclusive endpoints, leap day, unsold products, and zero-rate intervals.

All seven ordinary cases are visible samples or trials. The sole authenticated source example is preserved exactly with all three products, all three Sales rows, six ordered outputs, and the complete per-product explanation. Invented examples were relabeled as trials, the former hidden unsold-product case is visible, and the source-invalid two-Sales-rows-for-one-product case was replaced by a primary-key-valid interval covering all three report years.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode database problem 1384 and SQL/MySQL as the native environment. The candidate preserves the Product and Sales schemas, their primary keys, inclusive date endpoints, 2018-through-2020 domain, daily-rate multiplication, product name lookup, one row per overlapping product-year, required output columns, and required product/year ordering.

The protected app-local sql.sql and immutable leetcode.sql bound to verified submission 2068809662 remain byte-for-byte unchanged, as does submission.json. Their only reviewed executable difference remains the unavoidable SQLite-versus-MySQL date-function dialect. solution_variants.json continues to select the protected source; candidate.sql is separate and inert, with no remote-Accepted status inferred or recorded for it.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed both table schemas and primary keys, inclusive period endpoints, the daily sales meaning, the 2018-through-2020 date domain, per-product/year totals, four output columns, required ordering, one exact example with its complete explanation, five source tables, and no separate constraints, hints, notes, images, diagrams, or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 a794cc383a2ab1d78000ba017ca660009de22cef3108cdc2090b010e9dc54b04 and validates without errors.
